title: Chest Pain
chief_complaint: Acute chest pain — evaluate for STEMI
hpi_narrative: {{patient_name}} presents to the emergency department with acute chest pain. ECG shows ST-segment elevation in leads II, III, and aVF consistent with an inferior STEMI. Initiate ACS protocol: aspirin, P2Y12 inhibitor, high-intensity statin, cardiology consult, and emergent PCI.
case_summary:
Differential: Acute Aortic Dissection, Pulmonary embolism, Pericardial tamponade, Esophageal rupture.

The patient has an ST-elevated inferior myocardial infarction (STEMI). ST elevations will be present in leads II, III, and aVF. The patient should immediately be started on dual antiplatelet therapy (DAPT): Aspirin plus a P2Y12 inhibitor (Ticagrelor is preferred; Clopidogrel is also accepted). A beta blocker and atorvastatin should also be initiated. Cardiology should be consulted and percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) — angioplasty with stent placement — should be performed, as this is the preferred reperfusion strategy.

In the USMLE, immediate PCI is available, so fibrinolytic therapy is not required. If fibrinolysis is ordered, partial credit will be awarded, but full credit requires PCI as the preferred approach. Ticagrelor and Prasugrel are the preferred P2Y12 agents; Clopidogrel is acceptable for full credit. Heparin is optional in STEMI going to cath lab.
